flags: No road construction, campaign, naming origin or designation date is supplied. The history paragraph identifies changes in the corridor’s communities rather than claiming a road origin or an outlaw itinerary.
Official sources give 231 miles; material maps 244 miles. Used the official length and distinguished Highway 12’s U.S. 20 endpoint west of Jackson from the promotional endpoint near South Sioux City.

Dropped current claim that Niobrara’s second move followed a court ruling. The cached town article asserts that sequence but provides no decision or relocation record to check it against. The ruling’s scope and remedy cannot be verified here; retained only the twice-moved history and first flood.

Monowi’s sole-resident and officeholder claims are supported only by the saved encyclopedia article. It explains the 2020 count of two as a census privacy artifact; no independent current municipal record is cached.

Cache names the reservation Santee Indian Reservation in the highway article and Santee Sioux Reservation in tourism and lake articles. Used the highway article’s wording; no tribal self-description is cached.

Ponca park distance differs between the town article (two miles) and park article (four miles); omitted the distance. All existing landmark moments, coordinates and motifs retained. No other current claim dropped for lack of cache support.
